version.changelog: one answer per .env, on every platform

llm.summary: This skill coherently provides read-only VMware Log Insight searches, with disclosed local credential and audit files.

dimensions.detail: The skill reads potentially sensitive infrastructure logs from a user-configured appliance, which is expected for its purpose; TLS verification is enabled by default and the setup guide recommends read-only accounts.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation uses uv/PyPI and local configuration under ~/.vmware-log-insight; no artifact scripts, cron jobs, startup entries, or destructive install steps were present.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Instructions are scoped to VMware/vSphere/ESXi Log Insight use, include routing limits, and explicitly warn agents to treat log lines as untrusted data.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: It uses disclosed local state: config.yaml, .env for credentials, automatic b64 obfuscation/chmod of password entries, cached API sessions in process, and ~/.vmware/audit.db call records; this is not hidden background persistence.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is centralized VMware log search, aggregation, field discovery, version checks, and alert reads; the artifact and inspected package code expose only read-oriented Log Insight API operations.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you intend to let the agent read VMware Log Insight data. Use a least-privilege read-only service account, protect ~/.vmware-log-insight/.env and ~/.vmware/audit.db, prefer a secret manager over stored passwords, and leave TLS verification enabled except for controlled lab appliances.
llm.findings:
[PE2] expected: The cited chmod 600 text is file-permission hardening for the local .env file, not sudo/root execution or privilege escalation.
[PE3] expected: Credential use is disclosed and purpose-aligned for authenticating to the configured Log Insight appliance; the artifact also warns that b64 is obfuscation, not encryption.
[RA2] expected: The cited state files are local config, credential storage, and audit records; I found no cron, startup script, daemon, hidden worker, or unauthorized cross-session control.
